commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified, out_string() already knows the exact
string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of scanning
again in stream_zrun().

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including
non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

The bounded scan runs inline. A positive precision is stored
on the field flags as a cap.

Closes #23019

mprintf: use size_t width for the bare Windows %I modifier

The bare "%I" length modifier (without an explicit "32" or "64"
suffix) is Microsoft's non-standard way to size an integer conversion
to the platform's native pointer/size_t width: 4 bytes on 32-bit
Windows, 8 bytes on 64-bit Windows. parse_flags() instead based the
choice on SIZEOF_CURL_OFF_T, which is 8 on both, so on 32-bit Windows
a bare "%In"/"%Id"/"%Iu" was always treated as 8-byte wide. For "%n"
this made the MTYPE_INTPTR sink write an 8-byte int64_t through a
caller-supplied pointer to a 4-byte destination, corrupting adjacent
memory; for "%Id"/"%Iu" it fetched 8 bytes from the argument list
where the caller passed a 4-byte value.

Switch the bare "%I" case to SIZEOF_SIZE_T, matching the same pattern
already used for "%z". Explicit "%I32"/"%I64" are unaffected. curl's
own code does not use the bare "%I" modifier anywhere.

Added test 1451 for verification (Windows-only).

Reported-by: Joshua Rogers

An explicit string precision is a counted size_t byte cap.
Record it on the same field flags.

Closes #23030

mprintf: make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error

Previously they returned the number of characters it output at the time
of the error, but that is not only contrary to what POSIX does, it also
makes it next to impossible for a caller to know when for example the
output failed because out of disk space or similar.

Verified by test 2380

A string field that is not left-justified records that on the
field flags, next to the other string-length sources.

Closes #23112

coupling: The precision-%s scan in out_string() reads one byte past the cap only when at least two of three field flags are set, and each flag plus the scan that needs the other two is introduced by a different commit. e68dc1c stores FLAGS_STRCAP for a positive precision and inlines a scan whose window is hard+1 only if FLAGS_STRCAP and FLAGS_STRARG are both set; it never sets FLAGS_STRARG, so that commit alone still stops at the precision. 6cba6cf stores FLAGS_STRARG for an explicit precision (the size_t byte count) and adds a second scan that reads past the cap only if FLAGS_STRARG and FLAGS_STRFIELD are both set; FLAGS_STRFIELD is still unset, so this commit's own scan does not overread, but together with e68dc1c the first scan does. 65fd355 stores FLAGS_STRFIELD when the field is not left-justified and adds a third scan that reads past the cap only if FLAGS_STRCAP and FLAGS_STRFIELD are both set. Any pair is sufficient for curl_maprintf("%.*s", n, buf) with an n-byte non-terminated buffer: CAP+ARG uses the first scan, ARG+FIELD the second, CAP+FIELD the third. Deleting any one commit's added lines leaves the other pair's flag stores and scan in place, so the same call still reads str[n]. Deleting all but one leaves at most one flag set, every scan bound stays at the precision, and the read does not happen. Each scan clamps the copied length back to the precision, so a normal C string (NUL at or before the cap, or bytes still inside the object) prints exactly as before.
